the-complete-guide-to-airbnb-pricing-str.description: A fictional Airbnb pricing example compares occupancy, nightly rates, turnover costs and a limited cash balance, with CSV calculations and a blank review log.

sections.heading: Start with a dated calendar and a cost definition
paragraphs: A pricing review should state what a quoted rate is expected to cover, which dates are actually available, and which costs change with each stay. A higher nightly rate, higher occupancy and a higher cash balance are three different outcomes. None follows automatically from changing a setting.

The example below compares three invented operating scenarios for one 30-night period. All 30 nights are assumed available. Nights sold, booking counts and rates are independent scenario inputs, not predictions of how guests respond to a price. There is no market sample, client result or claim that one scenario can be achieved.

sections.heading: Three fictional scenarios: more nights can leave less cash
paragraphs: All amounts are fictional US dollars. The calculation assumes a 15.5% host service fee on accommodation revenue only, $30 of selected variable costs per sold night, $70 per completed stay for turnover, and $1,500 of selected fixed operating costs. Guest-paid cleaning and other host charges are zero. Taxes, refunds and currency effects are not modeled. Use the actual fee base and transaction fee for your listing rather than applying this assumption indiscriminately.

The final balance is before debt payments, income taxes, capital spending, replacement reserves and owner compensation. It is not net profit, distributable cash, or a return on an investment. Even the positive case may not fund those excluded requirements.

sections.heading: Read the result without turning assumptions into a forecast
paragraphs: Scenario B sells 22 nights at $140, compared with 18 nights at $160 in A. Its accommodation revenue is $200 higher, but the modeled fee rises $31, nightly costs rise $120, and five additional turnovers add $350. The balance therefore declines by $301: from negative $26.40 to negative $327.40. The higher occupancy does not make B the better cash result under these assumptions.

Scenario C has the highest rate and the fewest nights and turnovers, leaving $166 before the excluded costs. This does not prove that raising a rate produces C. The assumed 14 sold nights might not occur, and different stay patterns or costs can reverse the comparison. Keep the demand assumption separate from the arithmetic.

For this worksheet, accommodation revenue equals sold nights times average nightly rate; occupancy equals sold nights divided by available nights. Deduct the modeled host fee, sold-night costs, turnover costs and selected fixed costs to obtain the displayed balance. Reconcile actual statements before treating these categories as complete.

sections.heading: Confirm the actual fee and the guest-facing total
paragraphs: Airbnb publishes different fee structures and says it is transitioning home hosts toward a single host service fee. The single-fee guidance describes 15.5% for most hosts, with exceptions. Confirm the fee on the relevant reservation and check the current guidance; do not use an old blanket 3% assumption for every listing. Additional host charges can also affect the fee base.

Compare the guest-facing total for the same dates, length of stay and guest count, as well as the host payout. A cleaning charge paid by a guest is revenue and a separate turnover cost is an expense; omitting one side or counting it twice changes the model. Record refunds and adjustments separately.

sections.heading: Review discounts and calendar controls together
paragraphs: Airbnb Smart Pricing lets hosts set a minimum and maximum, but Airbnb states that discounts can take the guest price below the Smart Pricing minimum. Custom calendar prices, trip-length discounts and other controls therefore need review together. A minimum entered in one field is not a complete test of every bookable itinerary.

Before a proposed change, record the listing, dates, current settings, intended price, discounts, minimum stay and the guest-facing breakdown for representative itineraries. After a change, inspect those same itineraries. This checks what is offered; it does not establish that a booking or revenue increase will follow.

sections.heading: Use a review log with comparable periods
paragraphs: Keep a dated reason for each pricing change and the next review date. Preserve the prior settings and actual results. Note unavailable nights, owner blocks, local events, cancellations and changes to the listing, so a different calendar is not presented as a clean price experiment.

Compare sold nights, average rate, accommodation revenue, fee deductions, completed stays and the same cost categories. Separate observed results from a proposed scenario and from a budget. If observations are sparse, record the uncertainty rather than announcing an optimal rate or a fixed time to results. The downloadable blank record is intended for that review.

faqs.q: Does the highest occupancy produce the highest cash balance?
faqs.a: No. Fictional scenario B has the most sold nights and the highest accommodation revenue, but additional turnover and nightly costs leave the lowest modeled balance. Actual results depend on actual demand and costs.

faqs.q: Is the 15.5% fee a universal Airbnb fee?
faqs.a: No. It is the selected assumption in this example. Airbnb describes different structures and exceptions; use the actual fee and fee base for the relevant reservation and current listing.

faqs.q: Does a positive scenario balance mean the property is profitable?
faqs.a: No. This model excludes debt payments, income taxes, capital spending, replacement reserves and owner compensation. The displayed balance is incomplete for assessing overall profit or available owner cash.

faqs.q: Does a Smart Pricing minimum prevent every discounted price below it?
faqs.a: No. Airbnb states that discounts can take the guest price below the Smart Pricing minimum. Review the combined settings and actual guest-facing breakdown.

str-market-research-how-to-identify-your.title: STR Market Research: Address, Evidence and Operating Assumptions
str-market-research-how-to-identify-your.description: Research an STR address with permission records, comparable revenue definitions, geographic operating questions and two evidence worksheets. No city rankings or return promises.

sections.heading: Research the address and the proposed operation
paragraphs: A market label does not establish that a particular home can be operated as a short-term rental, that a quoted revenue number is comparable, or that the operating plan is affordable. Start a dated evidence record for the address, ownership arrangement and intended stay pattern. This guide offers a research process; it does not rank cities or report investment returns.

Earlier roundup URLs now lead to this guide because their repeated text contained no supported market rankings. No underlying market study or local dataset is being presented here. Keep observed facts, assumptions and unresolved questions in separate columns.

sections.heading: Permission is an address-level question
paragraphs: Identify the relevant local authority and preserve the current official rule, its effective date, and any written answer about the proposed use. Ask what approvals, inspections, occupancy restrictions, taxes and operating conditions apply. Separately review the lease, association restrictions and ownership arrangement with the appropriate parties. A neighboring listing or platform registration field is not confirmation for your address.

Airbnb’s city-regulations guidance points hosts toward local government and other applicable rules. It does not decide whether a specific property is eligible. If the evidence is missing or contradictory, mark the decision unresolved and identify who can answer it before relying on the operating plan.

sections.heading: Require a comparable revenue record
paragraphs: Record the source, reporting period, property type, size, guest capacity, availability definition and treatment of cancellations for each comparison. Separate advertised nightly prices, modeled estimates and documented completed-stay results. They answer different questions. A blocked calendar night does not by itself establish a paid booking.

Ask whether a revenue figure includes cleaning charges, other fees or taxes, and how many nights were available. Identify differences in amenities, location, restrictions and season. Do not convert a high advertised rate into an annual revenue forecast by assuming every available night sells. Use the pricing example linked below to see why more accommodation revenue can still leave a lower limited operating balance.

sections.heading: A fictional evidence screen, not a city ranking
paragraphs: Consider three invented candidates. Candidate A has a revenue spreadsheet but no confirmed answer about the proposed rental use: hold that question open. Candidate B has a current approval for a different ownership arrangement: hold until the applicable authority confirms what the proposed change requires. Candidate C has a confirmed restriction incompatible with the proposed use: stop relying on that STR operating plan unless the underlying facts or requirements legitimately change.

These examples contain no real addresses, legal determinations or investment recommendations. None is marked “approved to buy.” A completed permission review still leaves physical condition, financing, insurance, operating capacity and financial assumptions to assess. The fictional CSV records the evidence gaps; the blank worksheet is for the reader’s own dated research.

sections.heading: Beach and coastal properties: define the exposure and access questions
paragraphs: Identify the actual access route, shoreline proximity, property construction and local authority rather than treating “beach market” as a uniform category. Request property-specific hazard and insurance review, including coverage terms, exclusions, deductibles and operational interruption questions. Record who supplied each answer.

FEMA explains how to use its Flood Map Service Center for flood-hazard information. A map record is an input to review, not an insurance quote, a guarantee against loss, or proof that a rental use is permitted. Record the map product and date and bring unresolved interpretation questions to the relevant authority or professional.

sections.heading: Mountain properties: test the operating route across seasons
paragraphs: Ask how guests, cleaners and emergency services would reach the actual property under the conditions relevant to the intended operating season. Identify responsibility for access, road service, utilities and maintenance. Confirm the service area and response assumptions with local providers rather than copying a resort-wide occupancy claim.

Build the calendar around the dates that can actually be offered. Keep a proposed winter closure, maintenance block and an unconfirmed operating date distinct from a sold night. A scenic label does not resolve those calendar assumptions.

sections.heading: Lake properties: separate the home from water access rights
paragraphs: Identify what access, dock, parking or shared-facility rights are actually included and what restrictions apply to guests. Ask the relevant owner, association or authority to confirm the proposed use. Record seasonal availability and who maintains each feature.

Do not assume that a nearby home’s amenities or revenue apply because both listings mention the same lake. A comparison should explain whether the guest experience, accessible facilities and operating dates are genuinely comparable.

sections.heading: Urban properties: match the exact unit and building
paragraphs: Identify the jurisdiction, building, unit and proposed ownership or tenancy arrangement. Preserve the applicable building or association documents alongside the government review. Ask about guest access, parking, occupancy and any operating conditions relevant to that unit.

Separate a listing that operates under an owner-occupancy arrangement from a proposed non-owner-occupied operation. Similar bedrooms and proximity to an attraction do not establish equivalent permission or economics.

sections.heading: Desert properties: define equipment and service assumptions
paragraphs: Request a property-specific assessment of the systems and amenities the operating plan depends on. Record maintenance responsibilities, service availability and any seasonal limitations. A pool, cooling system or outdoor feature appearing in a listing does not establish its condition, running cost or permitted use.

NOAA’s Storm Events Database provides historical event records. Use the documented location, period and reporting scope as context; it does not forecast bookings, measure a particular building’s condition or establish future losses. Keep an insurer’s or inspector’s specific assessment separate from regional historical data.

sections.heading: Compare the cash requirements, not an affordability label
paragraphs: Separate acquisition cash, launch work, operating costs, turnover costs, financing obligations and reserves in the proposed plan. Ask which items are supported by a quote or actual statement and which remain assumptions. A lower purchase price or larger gross revenue estimate does not by itself establish more owner cash.

Keep appreciation assumptions outside the operating cash calculation. Record the holding period, possible sale costs and the source of any proposed value change separately. This guide supplies no appreciation forecast, market-wide return or loan-qualification determination.

sections.heading: Date the evidence and revisit changes
paragraphs: Keep the rule version, dataset period, quote date and person confirming each material item. Record proposed changes as proposed, not enacted. A prior-year roundup title should not substitute for current evidence.

Before advancing the plan, list the remaining questions, their responsible reviewers and the decisions they affect. When a material condition changes, revisit the affected permission, operating or financial assumptions. An evidence record supports a review; it does not replace it.

faqs.q: Does this guide rank the best STR cities?
faqs.a: No. It provides an evidence-led research process and geographic screening questions. It contains no ranked market dataset or expected investment return.

faqs.q: Does another listing prove that my address can host short stays?
faqs.a: No. Confirm the actual address, proposed arrangement and current applicable requirements with the relevant parties. Treat missing evidence as unresolved.

faqs.q: Is a high nightly rate the same as strong annual cash flow?
faqs.a: No. Available nights, sold nights, fees, turnovers, operating costs and excluded obligations affect the calculation. Advertised rates and modeled estimates are not completed-stay results.
